# The reasons a test may skip on the `stock` cell, beyond the common ones in
# .github/expected-skips.txt: the hosted image as shipped, which the `defaults`
# cell sets back to a stock kernel's defaults. Each line is a privilege this
# cell does not grant, read off run 36606817052 (docs/portability.md, "The
# fourteenth wave").
#
# Adding a line is a claim about the cell. Say which, above the line.

# perf_event_paranoid 4: every perf event is refused to an unprivileged
# process, its own counters included, and the probes name the sysctl.
perf_event_paranoid is [3-9]
# AppArmor's user-namespace restriction (apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns
# 1): `unshare -Urm` cannot write its uid map, so the scenarios that build a
# device, a namespace or a /proc/diskstats of their own inside one skip.
`unshare -Urm` is refused here
an unprivileged user namespace
# The job runs in root's service cgroup, which delegates nothing to the
# runner's user: no cgroup of its own, and no controller below it.
cannot create a cgroup under
this user cannot create a cgroup under its own slice
delegates the (memory|cpu|io|pids) controller to this user
omn-scenario-[a-z]+` could not be created
# The same sysctl, as the probes word it without "is" (run 37f17c8).
perf_event_paranoid [3-9]
# paranoid 4 refuses every perf event to an unprivileged process: the software
# cpu clock, a context-switch counter on its own pid, a sampling unwinder's
# open. The tests quote the kernel's refusal, which names nothing else.
refuses the software cpu clock to this process
was refused \(Permission denied \(os error 13\)\); check /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid
perf_event_open: Permission denied \(os error 13\)
# Root's service cgroup, which hands no controller down to the runner's user.
no ancestor of `/system.slice/[^`]+` that this user owns hands the (cpu|memory|io|pids) controller down
